title: Residential energy consumption dynamics: A SHAP-based interpretation, k-means clustering, and predictive modelling
abstract: A proper understanding of climatic consumption dynamics is critical for demand-side management, grid stability, and climate-sensitive residential energy planning. The non-linear interaction between meteorological conditions has necessitated intelligent predictive models. However, existing studies focused on machine learning (ML) models in their black-box nature, with limited interpretability of the impact of climatic-drivers, climatic-demand interactions, and hidden consumption regimes. This research fills this gap through an integrated framework that combines seasonal hypothesis-testing, k-means clustering, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based interpretability, and advanced predictive modeling using XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), long-short term memory (LSTM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Autoregressive Integrated moving average (ARIMA). The seasonal hypothesis-testing using ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD revealed statistically significant differences in energy consumption across seasons, with peak-demand during winter and summer extremes. SHAP-based feature ranking identified temperature and humidity as the most influential drivers of electricity-demand. The k-means clustering revealed three distinct groups/clusters, which reflect the climatic-consumption scenarios. The ensemble learning (RF and XGBoost) exhibited the lowest training-error. RF had the best training performance with MSE, RMSE, and MAE values of 1.6484, 1.2839, and 0.8480. The data-driven insights in this study provide useful intelligence that supports critical decision-making through a proper understanding of the residential climatic-consumption dynamics. • ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD revealed a significant difference in consumption across seasons • k-means clustering reveals 3 distinct climatic-consumption patterns and regimes • SHAP revealed temperature as a dominant consumption driver • The random forest gave the best training performance with RMSE = 1.2839 • The framework facilitates climate-sensitive demand-side management and planning.

title: Synergistic hybrid systems of 2D-MOFs and TMDs for advanced energy harvesting
abstract: The globally trending move towards renewable energy sources requires materials capable of harvesting, storing, and converting energy in a competent fashion and yet scalable, robust, and affordable. Two-dimensional metal-organic frameworks (2D-MOFs) and transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have been promising materials for photovoltaics, thermoelectrics, piezoelectrics, and triboelectrics, respectively, but both material families are plagued by intrinsic drawbacks. MOFs have high area and chemical tailoring but are hampered by low conductivity, and TMDs have robust electronic and catalytic functionality but are plagued by stability and scalability issues. Recent developments indicate hybrid 2D-MOF/TMD systems are capable of offsetting failings by encapsulating complementary properties, facilitating superior charge separation, band alignment engineering, and enhancement in environmental tolerance. This review critically examines the structural, electronic, and functional synergies of 2D-MOF/TMD hybrids with emphasis on synthesis strategies, interface engineering, defect modulation, and emerging applications in diverse energy harvesting platforms. Comparative analyses of existing studies highlight how hybrid architectures deliver higher power densities, longer cycling stability, and superior device integration relative to their parent materials. Critical issues such as scalable synthesis, long-term stability under operating conditions, and reproducible device-level integration are also mentioned as hurdles in commercialization. Experimental design, computational modeling, and machine learning are envisaged in the future to accelerate discovery and optimization of high-performance hybrids. Bridging the gap between applied engineering and basic research, 2D-MOF/TMD hybrids are a paradigm shift in multifunctional materials and a promising avenue towards next-generation sustainable energy technology.

ai4s_review.rationale: 摘要仅将ML写作未来方向，但公开正文§4.4（PDF第20—21页）实质讨论InterMat的DFT+GNN界面/能带预测，以及KNN/SVM相稳定性筛选，故按AI参与能源材料预测的实质综述纳入。依据正文内容而非标题或未来愿景；不声称该综述新训练模型，也不把普通DFT本身称AI。

Comparative analyses of existing studies highlight how hybrid architectures deliver higher power densities, longer cycling stability, and superior device integration relative to their parent materials. Critical issues such as scalable synthesis, long-term stability under operating conditions, and reproducible device-level integration are also mentioned as hurdles in commercialization. Experimental design, computational modeling, and machine learning are envisaged in the future to accelerate discovery and optimization of high-performance hybrids. Bridging the gap between applied engineering and basic research, 2D-MOF/TMD hybrids are a paradigm shift in multifunctional materials and a promising avenue towards next-generation sustainable energy technology.

title: Battery thermal management of electric vehicles: A review and bibliometric analysis of liquid cooling methods
abstract: Thermal management plays a vital role in the operation of electric vehicle (EV) batteries, directly influencing their efficiency, safety, and market adoption. In real-world EV operation, inadequate thermal regulation can accelerate battery degradation and increase safety risks, highlighting the importance of effective battery thermal management system (BTMS) design. In response, extensive research explored liquid BTMSs for EV applications. Despite this growing body of research, a comprehensive overview that combines a critical review and a bibliometric analysis of EV liquid BTMS research remains scarce. This paper aims to address this gap by presenting a combined critical review and bibliometric investigation of recent trends and developments in EV liquid BTMSs. The review examines key aspects of liquid BTMSs, including system configurations, coolant types, performance enhancement methods, and hybrid configurations. The bibliometric analysis covers research and review publications included in the Scopus database from 2015 to 2025, extracted on the 29 th of October 2025. The technical review was updated separately to include selected 2026 publications. After screening, 472 publications strongly related to liquid BTMSs were identified. The analysis demonstrates continuous growth in the field with an annual growth rate of 40.97% and a low average document age of 3.19 years. China leads the research with 214 publications. Liquid BTMS keyword analysis highlights three main research themes: temperature control and coolant systems, EV applications and battery technologies, and battery modeling and simulation. Key research gaps include coupled electrothermal modeling and artificial intelligence-based predictive control. This review highlights recent advancements and research gaps that can guide future development of liquid BTMS design and optimization to improve EV performance and safety.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Performance Prediction and Parameter Identification of Microbial Fuel Cells
abstract: Bioelectrochemical systems (BES) such as microbial fuel cells (MFCs) offer a promising route for sustainable wastewater treatment and bioelectricity generation. However, MFC modeling faces a structural dichotomy: mechanistic models provide physical interpretability but suffer from difficult calibration, while data-driven approaches offer predictive flexibility at the cost of mechanistic transparency and limited extrapolation. To reconcile these paradigms, we developed BioElec-PINN, a physics-informed neural network framework that couples sparse experimental data with a differential-algebraic bioelectrochemical model that distinguishes bulk and biofilm substrate compartments through a mass-transfer coefficient. This paper presents the BioElec-PINN architecture and evaluates its performance on fed-batch MFCs treating synthetic winery wastewater across varying organic loads. We trained the network to jointly reconstruct model-conditioned latent states and estimate ten regularized cycle-specific kinetic, transport, and electrochemical parameters. The BioElec-PINN achieved calibration voltage normalized root mean square error NRMSE values of 0.048–0.100. The inferred parameter sets were subsequently transferred without recalibration to a Radau IIA solver (classical solver), whose forward trajectories showed close cycle-level agreement and supported the cross-formulation dynamic consistency of the learned mechanistic parameterization. A matched Direct multilayer perceptron MLP was additionally evaluated using an interleaved held-out protocol in which approximately 40% of the observations were retained for training and the remaining 60% were used exclusively for raw-data evaluation. The Direct MLP achieved lower pointwise interpolation errors, with mean voltage and chemical oxygen demand (COD) NRMSE values of 0.064 and 0.146, compared with 0.121 and 0.206 for the BioElec-PINN, respectively. A conditional residual-bootstrap analysis based on 20 complete BioElec-PINN retrainings was used to quantify parameter uncertainty. Thirty-three of the forty cycle-specific estimates exhibited relative 95% interval widths below 1%, while the bootstrap correlation structure revealed coordinated kinetic, mediator, and electrochemical parameter groups. However, the unconstrained MLP introduced non-monotonic COD trajectories in three cycles and physically inadmissible continuation outside the observed interval, including negative voltage and substantial COD rebound. In contrast, the BioElec-PINN preserved monotonic substrate depletion and coupled voltage–substrate dynamics while reconstructing model-conditioned latent states and estimating regularized cycle-specific effective parameters. The framework therefore provides a physically structured inverse-calibration component for future MFC digital twins, with raw-data performance, physical admissibility, parameter transferability, and conditional uncertainty evaluated explicitly.

title: A comprehensive review of hydrogen integrated hybrid renewable energy systems: Configurations, models, simulation and optimization with artificial intelligence
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive review of hydrogen-based hybrid renewable energy systems (HRESs), covering mathematical models, simulation and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven optimization approaches. Emphasizing the potential of hydrogen as an energy carrier to deepen renewable energy integration, especially in solar and wind HRESs, this review systematically details mathematical models for various renewable generation and storage systems, serving as a structured reference for researchers. Given the complexity of HRES modeling, this work provides insights into different modeling software and optimization algorithms, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence methods. The integration of software and artificial intelligence promises to solve complex modeling and optimization challenges with potential applications in different environments. Future directions suggest that the physical model-assisted AI framework, which embeds physical principles within AI models, holds promise for enhancing prediction accuracy and reliability in HRES applications. This framework, especially when combined with stochastic optimization, offers a potential pathway to address challenges in data availability and computational complexity, supporting the effective design and optimization of hydrogen-based HRESs for real-world applications. The overall findings will help improve the design and optimization of hydrogen-based hybrid renewable energy systems for practical implementation.

title: Rock mechanics–driven interpretable machine learning framework for preliminary seal integrity screening in geological CO2 storage
abstract: Caprock integrity assessment is essential for ensuring the long-term security of geological CO 2 storage; however, early-stage evaluation is often challenged by limited and heterogeneous subsurface datasets. This study proposes an interpretable machine learning framework for preliminary caprock integrity screening using limited rock mechanics data from the 31/5–7 Eos well-core of the Northern Lights CO 2 storage project. An unsupervised learning workflow was first employed to reconstruct Safe, Transitional, and Risk integrity regimes through cluster validation and ambiguity-based boundary analysis. Multiple supervised learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost, were subsequently developed and evaluated under stratified train/test split, Leave-One-Out Cross Validation (LOOCV), and repeated stratified cross-validation strategies. Random Forest demonstrated the most stable predictive behaviour across validation schemes, achieving balanced accuracies exceeding 0.86. Explainability analyses using Random Forest feature importance and SHAP consistently identified porosity and axial stress as dominant screening controls, suggesting coupled stress–structure interactions govern integrity behaviour within the studied dataset. Based on these observations, a Stress–Porosity Screening Score (SPSS) was developed as a simplified post hoc screening descriptor for rapid integrity evaluation. Statistical analyses demonstrated significant differentiation of SPSS across reconstructed integrity regimes ( p < 0.001). Decision-tree interpretation further enabled extraction of preliminary data-emergent screening pathways and threshold behaviour. Conclusively, the proposed methodology provides an interpretable and data-adaptive screening approach intended to support early-stage caprock assessment and guide subsequent detailed geomechanical investigations.

title: Emerging noble-metal-free catalysts for hydrogen technologies: Bridging theory and practice
abstract: Noble-metal-free catalysts are emerging as cost-effective, durable, and scalable alternatives to platinum-group metals (PGMs). This review surveys advances across four domains: computation, production, storage, and conversion. Computational methods, including density functional theory and machine learning, accelerate discovery by predicting adsorption energetics, identifying active sites, and guiding operando characterization. In hydrogen production, carbon materials, transition-metal oxides, phosphides, and single-atom frameworks enable efficient thermocatalytic, electrocatalytic, and photocatalytic processes, narrowing the gap with PGMs. In hydrogen storage, porous adsorbents, solid-state hydrides, and liquid organic hydrogen carriers are re-engineered with earth-abundant catalysts to improve kinetics, reversibility, and durability. In hydrogen conversion, heteroatom-doped carbons, transition-metal alloys, and M–N–C single-atom catalysts show competitive activity for the oxygen reduction and hydrogen oxidation reactions. Hybrid systems that combine trace PGMs with non-precious elements offer pragmatic pathways to commercialization. By integrating theoretical insight with experimental validation, these studies establish design principles that link electronic structure, microstructure, and performance. The target audience includes researchers and practitioners in catalysis, materials science, and energy engineering. This review provides a framework for translating noble-metal-free catalysts into scalable hydrogen technologies and reinforces hydrogen’s role as a cornerstone of the global energy transition.

title: Recent advances in the application of high-entropy materials in lithium-based anodes
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries constitute the cornerstone of modern energy storage. However, commercial graphite anodes are increasingly limited by their theoretical capacity and energy density. Although high-capacity alternatives such as silicon and transition metal oxides have been explored, their practical implementation remains severely bottlenecked by structural instability. High-entropy materials (HEMs) have emerged as promising candidates capable of transcending these conventional limitations. Governed by the four fundamental core effects, HEMs exhibit unique synergistic attributes, including enhanced lattice resilience and superior electrochemical kinetics, that surpass those of conventional binary or ternary counterparts. This review systematically evaluates recent progress in HEM-based anodes for lithium storage, categorizing high-entropy alloys, oxides, and burgeoning derivatives, including sulfides and phosphides. We further dissect the multifaceted storage mechanisms and the practical hurdles facing the predominant high-entropy oxide anodes. Finally, we offer forward-looking perspectives on the field, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) for accelerated material discovery and the pathways toward industrial-scale application.

title: Machine learning interatomic potentials: A new tool for developing high-entropy perovskites for solid oxide fuel cells, protonic ceramic fuel cells and beyond
abstract: High-entropy perovskites (HEPs) have emerged as promising cathode candidates for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) and protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) as they combine thermodynamic stabilization through configurational entropy with tunable transport and electrocatalytic properties. However, the vast compositional space renders empirical trial-and-error discovery prohibitively slow. In this perspective, we argue that an integrated computational pipeline, comprising machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) coupled with Bayesian optimization for multi-objective compositional search, can significantly accelerate the rational design of SOFC and PCFC cathodes. We describe how MLIPs can be leveraged to obtain defect energetics for HEP cathodes. Then, we outline how Bayesian optimization navigates the resulting high-dimensional property landscape to identify Pareto-optimal compositions balancing key functional properties. Finally, we propose promising research directions for catalyzing rapid and reproducible discovery of cathodes in fuel cells and beyond.

title: Advancing energy accessibility, equity, and sustainability with city information model for renewable, storage and infrastructure
abstract: The accelerating transition towards low-carbon and resilient urban energy systems requires integrated approaches that simultaneously address renewable energy deployment, energy storage, infrastructure optimization, and the social dimensions of energy accessibility and equity. This review examines the emerging role of the City Information Model (CIM) as a comprehensive digital framework for enabling data-driven planning, analysis, and governance of urban energy systems. CIM integrates multi-source urban data—including geospatial information, building characteristics, infrastructure networks, and real-time energy flows—into a unified platform, supporting holistic decision-making across sectors. The paper synthesizes recent advances in the application of CIM for planning and operation of renewable energy systems. It highlights how CIM facilitates system-level optimization, scenario simulation, and infrastructure coordination, particularly when combined with digital twin technologies, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things. Beyond technical integration, the review emphasizes the critical role of CIM in enhancing energy accessibility by identifying underserved areas and enabling targeted infrastructure investments. It further explores how CIM-driven analytics can support equity-oriented policies by incorporating socio-economic indicators, thereby addressing energy poverty and promoting inclusive energy transitions. The review also discusses key challenges, including data interoperability, standardization, governance, and privacy concerns. CIM is positioned as an effective tool for advancing renewable energy integration, infrastructure resilience, and socially inclusive urban energy systems, contributing to the broader goals of sustainability and equitable development.

title: Biomass-derived carbon electrocatalysts for zinc-air Batteries: A review of design strategies, machine learning acceleration, and future perspectives
abstract: The practical application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (R-ZABs) is critically limited by high-performance bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, as their intrinsic activity directly governs the efficiency and longevity of air cathodes. Recently, biomass-derived carbon materials are compelling candidates for bifunctional electrocatalysts, benefiting from their renewable nature, low cost, inherently porous architecture, and naturally doped heteroatoms. Understanding the structural design principles of biomass-derived carbon electrocatalysts is therefore essential for advancing the performance of R-ZABs. Based on this understanding, this review first introduces the fundamental configuration, reaction mechanisms, and challenges for R-ZABs to understand the cathodic catalyst design criteria. Furthermore, the diverse precursor sources of biomass materials are summarized and categorized. Moreover, the design strategies for biomass-derived carbon catalysts, including metal-free, single-atom, and transition-metal-compound decorations, as well as integrated air cathodes, are summarized to achieve high activity and long-term stability in R-ZABs. Notably, machine learning has gradually been applied to the high-throughput catalyst design and optimization due to its advantages in efficiently analyzing structure-performance relationships and accurately predicting catalytic activity. Finally, the critical challenges of biomass-derived carbon electrocatalysts, together with the future perspectives for R-ZABs, are thoroughly emphasized. This review aims to guide the development of biomass-derived carbon electrocatalysts for next-generation R-ZABs.

title: Advanced engineering of inorganic semiconductor nanowires: Materials-by-design for next-generation green energy technologies
abstract: Inorganic semiconductor nanowires (NWs) provide an unusually versatile platform for green-energy technologies because composition, crystal phase, defects, interfaces, morphology, and dimensionality can be engineered across multiple length scales. This review critically examines how these coupled design variables govern charge generation and transport, surface recombination, catalytic activity, ion diffusion, thermal transport, and operational stability. Rather than cataloguing individual materials, we identify transferable structure–property–performance relationships across photovoltaics, photoelectrochemical water splitting, photocatalysis, electrochemical energy storage, and thermoelectric conversion. A central conclusion is that nanoscale advantages are intrinsically conditional: reduced dimensions can enhance light trapping, carrier collection, reaction kinetics, and strain accommodation, but simultaneously intensify surface recombination, interfacial instability, defect sensitivity, and integration losses. We therefore evaluate competing engineering strategies in terms of these trade-offs and their implications for device-scale performance, durability, manufacturability, and sustainability. Recent advances in operando characterization, multiscale simulation, density functional theory, machine learning, and active learning are further assessed as tools for connecting synthesis conditions with experimentally validated material states and functional performance. Particular attention is given to the remaining gap between idealized computational predictions and structurally complex experimental NWs. Finally, we identify reproducibility, standardized data, device integration, scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and uncertainty-aware human-supervised automation as critical requirements for translating semiconductor NWs from laboratory optimization toward deployable green-energy systems.

This review critically examines how these coupled design variables govern charge generation and transport, surface recombination, catalytic activity, ion diffusion, thermal transport, and operational stability. Rather than cataloguing individual materials, we identify transferable structure–property–performance relationships across photovoltaics, photoelectrochemical water splitting, photocatalysis, electrochemical energy storage, and thermoelectric conversion. A central conclusion is that nanoscale advantages are intrinsically conditional: reduced dimensions can enhance light trapping, carrier collection, reaction kinetics, and strain accommodation, but simultaneously intensify surface recombination, interfacial instability, defect sensitivity, and integration losses. We therefore evaluate competing engineering strategies in terms of these trade-offs and their implications for device-scale performance, durability, manufacturability, and sustainability. Recent advances in operando characterization, multiscale simulation, density functional theory, machine learning, and active learning are further assessed as tools for connecting synthesis conditions with experimentally validated material states and functional performance. Particular attention is given to the remaining gap between idealized computational predictions and structurally complex experimental NWs. Finally, we identify reproducibility, standardized data, device integration, scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and uncertainty-aware human-supervised automation as critical requirements for translating semiconductor NWs from laboratory optimization toward deployable green-energy systems.

title: Energy security in transition: Multi-Scale risks, metrics, and circular bio-resources from Europe to the Bavarian region of Germany
abstract: ABSTRACT This article reviews how energy security is being reconceptualised and practiced in the context of Europe’s low-carbon transition, with a particular focus on Germany and the state of Bavaria, and on the role of circular bio-resources converted by thermo-chemical-conversion technologies. A targeted review of recent peer-reviewed work was undertaken using major bibliographic databases, complemented by a critical appraisal of widely used indicator frameworks and composite indices, and by a spatially explicit assessment of bio-waste and sewage-sludge conversion potential in Bavaria using Thermo-Catalytic Reforming (TCR®) as an illustrative technology. The synthesis shows that the dominant understanding of energy security has shifted from narrow fuel-supply concerns to broader socio-technical concepts that link security to sustainability, risk, equity and digitalisation. However, prevailing indices remain strongly supply- and price-oriented, rely on overlapping indicators and weakly justified weights, and only partially capture environmental, social and technological dimensions. At the European level, diversification of energy mixes, improvements in energy and carbon intensity, and expansion of renewables have improved several aspects of security, yet high import dependence and new vulnerabilities associated with gas trade, critical materials and concentrated low-carbon technology supply chains persist. Germany’s Energiewende has raised the share of renewables and reduced coal use, but the simultaneous nuclear phase-out and former reliance on Russian pipeline gas have created a complex risk profile in which system flexibility, storage, hydrogen and bioenergy become central levers. The Bavarian case underlines that energy security is strongly region-specific: high industrial demand, heterogeneous renewable resources, land-use and biodiversity constraints, water stress and local acceptance shape feasible pathways. Across all scales, the growing use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence offers powerful capabilities for forecasting, clustering and operational security, but also introduces cyber and governance risks. Overall, the review argues for explicitly risk-oriented, multi-scale energy-security metrics and scenarios that embed climate-neutrality, justice and water-energy-food nexus constraints; for systematic integration of circular bio-resource and thermo-chemical pathways into regional and national planning; and for treating digitalisation and ’Artificial Intelligence’ (AI) as core dimensions of energy security rather than neutral enablers.

title: Advances in MXene-Enabled triboelectric nanogenerators: From material chemistry to emerging applications
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as a promising technology for harvesting ubiquitous mechanical energy and enabling self-powered electronic systems. However, achieving high output performance, long-term stability, and environmental robustness remains a critical challenge, largely governed by the intrinsic properties of triboelectric materials. Recently, MXenes, a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, have attracted significant attention for TENG applications owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, mechanical flexibility, and abundant functional groups. This review presents a comprehensive and critical assessment of MXene-enabled TENGs, covering representative materials including Ti 3 C 2 T x , Ti 3 CNT x , Nb 2 CT x , Mo 2 CT x , and V 2 CT x . This review systematically analyzes their synthesis routes, structural features, interfacial properties, and multifunctional roles in device architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on the mechanisms by which MXenes enhance triboelectric performance through dielectric modulation, charge trapping, suppression of charge recombination, moisture resistance, and enlarged effective contact area. Their versatility enables deployment as conductive electrodes, triboelectric active layers, nanocomposite reinforcements, and interfacial charge-management components. Furthermore, this review highlights emerging applications in wearable electronics, human–machine interfaces, biomedical sensing, intelligent monitoring systems, and artificial intelligence-assisted platforms. Despite remarkable advances, key challenges related to oxidation susceptibility, scalable manufacturing, cost-effectiveness, and power-density optimization continue to limit practical deployment. Finally, this study identifies critical research opportunities and future directions for MXene engineering, device design, and system integration. By elucidating the fundamental interactions between MXenes and triboelectric systems, this review establishes a roadmap for the development of high-performance, durable, and application-ready next-generation TENG technologies.

title: Integrated dual photocatalysts for simultaneous solar hydrogen production and CO2 capture-conversion: Design principles, mechanistic insights and future perspectives
abstract: The global pursuit of carbon neutrality has accelerated the development of sustainable technologies that simultaneously address clean energy production and greenhouse gas mitigation. Solar-driven hydrogen (H 2 ) production and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) capture-conversion are widely recognized as complementary approaches; however, most studies and existing reviews have examined these processes independently, resulting in fragmented catalyst design and limited understanding of their synergistic integration. To address this gap, this review critically evaluates the emerging field of integrated photocatalyst systems capable of coupling solar H 2 evolution with CO 2 capture and photoconversion within a unified catalytic platform. A systematic literature survey of peer-reviewed publications published between 2015 and 2026 was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and SpringerLink to assess recent advances in multifunctional photocatalysts. The review examines semiconductor heterojunctions, graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 )-based composites, layered double hydroxides, transition-metal sulfides, MXenes, metal-organic frameworks, perovskite oxynitrides and single-atom catalysts, with emphasis on the roles of band structure engineering, defect modulation, interfacial charge transfer, active-site regulation and surface chemistry in enhancing dual-function catalytic performance. Critical analysis reveals that synergistic band alignment, efficient charge separation and engineered catalytic interfaces are the primary factors governing simultaneous H 2 evolution and CO 2 conversion, whereas photocorrosion, catalyst durability, product selectivity and reactor-scale integration remain the major barriers to practical implementation. Unlike previous reviews that separately address hydrogen evolution or CO 2 reduction, this work establishes a unified framework integrating catalyst design principles, mechanistic insights, quantitative performance comparisons, stability considerations and techno-economic perspectives. Finally, emerging opportunities in defect engineering, operando characterization, machine-learning-assisted catalyst discovery and integrated solar photoreactor design are highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation photocatalytic systems for sustainable solar fuel production and carbon-neutral energy technologies.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning empowered surface growth of 2D materials: Synthesis, characterization and mechanism
verified_metadata.abstract: The advent of atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) materials provides a versatile platform to transcend the fundamental limitations of silicon-based electronics and continue the miniaturization of field-effect transistors, yet the epitaxial growth of wafer-scale, single-crystalline structure remains a formidable challenge. In recent years, the vigorous development of machine learning (ML) techniques has contributed to a revolutionary shift in materials synthesis, characterization and application, offering unprecedented opportunities for scientific and technological innovations that are inaccessible through traditional experimental and computational methods. This review aims to outline recent progress of ML-assisted 2D materials growth, including optimizing synthesis conditions, automating real-time characterizations and unveiling growth mechanisms. Current challenges and future prospects in this frontier research field are also discussed. Overall, this review highlights the synergy between advanced ML techniques and surface growth approaches for accelerated materials synthesis and intelligent design of next-generation functional devices.

verified_metadata.title: Theoretical insights into intermetallic compound surfaces in hydrogen-involving catalytic reactions
verified_metadata.abstract: Intermetallic compounds, long regarded primarily from a metallurgical perspective, are now rapidly emerging as a versatile class of catalytic materials. Their well-ordered atomic structure and distinctive electronic structures – compared to those of their constituent elements – endow them with unique advantages, particularly in terms of stability and selectivity. However, the rational design of intermetallic catalysts remains highly challenging. In this review, we focus on theoretical approaches, namely the modeling of these materials and their catalytic properties, primarily using density functional theory, with an outlook toward emerging machine learning methods. Special attention is given to hydrogenation reactions, which are central to sustainable chemical processes. Finally, general trends are discussed and future perspectives are outlined.

title: Peptide screening, design, and application for detecting small-molecule contaminants in food
abstract: Small-molecule contaminants (SMCs), including pesticides, veterinary drugs, mycotoxins, and heavy metals, threaten food safety and human health. Traditional detection methods such as chromatography and immunoassays are accurate but costly, time-consuming, and less practical for rapid screening. Peptides have emerged as promising alternatives because of their small size, modifiability, high specificity, and compatibility with sensor platforms. This review integrates developments in traditional peptide screening, computational design, and analytical applications for detecting SMCs in food. It critically evaluates the strengths and limitations of current methods while exploring how artificial intelligence and nanomaterial-based strategies enhance peptide performance. By bridging peptide engineering and analytical chemistry, this review provides practical insights for developing rapid, cost-effective, and sensitive detection tools. It also identifies knowledge gaps and future opportunities, guiding both experienced researchers and newcomers to advance peptide-based assays toward real-world applications in food safety and environmental monitoring.

title: From soils to edible tissues: Critical assessment of techniques for detecting micro- and nanoplastics in agroecosystems
abstract: The rapid accumulation of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) in agricultural landscapes has raised urgent questions about their fate in soils, their transfer to plants, and their eventual entry into human diets. While early reviews of MNPs in food matrices, soils, and plants provided important foundations, most treated these compartments separately and rarely aligned analytical evidence across the soil-plant-edible tissue continuum. This review synthesizes current knowledge along the agricultural soil-plant-food pathway, with emphasis on analytical workflows such as sampling, pretreatment, spectroscopic imaging, and thermoanalytical and mass-spectrometric quantification. We critically evaluate detection limits, recovery biases, and the suitability of these methods for complex agricultural matrices, while also highlighting emerging computational tools for particle recognition, automated spectral deconvolution, and improved mass-balance closure. Persistent challenges involving sub-50 µm fractions, nanoscale particles, and environmentally realistic concentrations are discussed. While earlier essential studies are included for context, the focus is on recent literature that captures the rapid evolution of analytical capabilities from 2020 to 2025. Linking field surveys, controlled uptake studies, and exposure modelling shows how harmonized protocols and improved QA/QC can strengthen dietary risk assessment. The review concludes by identifying methodological gaps and introducing recent advances in analytical determination, including advanced imaging techniques such as confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLMS) or photo-induced force microscopy (PiFM), thermoanalytical MS (e.g., pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), thermal extraction and desorption (TED)-GC/MS and fast-MS platforms), and imaging-enhanced Raman/Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), together with novel data analysis workflows that now warrant an integrated appraisal focused on agroecosystems. title: CRISPR-powered biosensors for metal ion monitoring: From molecular recognition to environmental applications
abstract: Heavy metals in the environment are harmful both to human beings and the environment. In the past, heavy metal contamination was detected using traditional analytical methods that were time-consuming, costly, and required complex equipment. In recent years, several different types of biosensors based upon the programmable use of nucleic acids have been developed. The focus of this review is to cover the architecture, principles of operation, and performance characteristics of CRISPR-based biosensors for detection of heavy metals. CRISPR-Cas12 and Cas13 nucleases enable programmable biosensors through collateral trans-cleavage of single-stranded DNA and RNA, respectively. The review further explores the conversion of specific heavy metal binding events into nucleic acid signals and their subsequent integration with CRISPR based molecular system. In addition, many different types of signal transduction modalities), and the use of nanomaterials for signal enhancement for heavy metals are also analysed. Presently, the available technologies demonstrates good recovery rates and comparable performance to ICP-MS for metal detection in complex matrix. Nonetheless, substantial challenges persists, including matrix interference from organic matter and competing ions, component stability and scalability, and regulatory standardisation. Future efforts are likely to include the development of portable devices integrated with smartphones, multiplex detection, microfluidic lab-on-a-chip integration, and the implementation of artificial intelligence to assist in data analysis. This article presents a thorough roadmap for converting laboratory advances into dependable technology capable of providing comprehensive monitoring of heavy metals for use in the field while stressing the need for ongoing optimisation with real-world sample matrices.

ai4s_review.rationale: 文献类型为正式综述，但全文的AI内容集中在Future perspectives and emerging directions下的Artificial intelligence and machine learning assisted analysis及结语，主要以may/will/could描述LSTM、分类、矩阵干扰校正和云/边缘平台的未来用途。已核该完整段落及其参考98/99（蛋白质谱分解、转基因大豆数字PCR），未显示CRISPR重金属检测中实质已开展AI研究的案例或评价；不能把列出模型名及未经目标场景支撑的近100%准确率描述当作AI4S实质贡献。按现有完整正文证据排除，CRISPR/核酸可编程或常规信号放大本身不等同AI。

Nonetheless, substantial challenges persists, including matrix interference from organic matter and competing ions, component stability and scalability, and regulatory standardisation. Future efforts are likely to include the development of portable devices integrated with smartphones, multiplex detection, microfluidic lab-on-a-chip integration, and the implementation of artificial intelligence to assist in data analysis. This article presents a thorough roadmap for converting laboratory advances into dependable technology capable of providing comprehensive monitoring of heavy metals for use in the field while stressing the need for ongoing optimisation with real-world sample matrices.

verified_metadata.title: From laboratory to real water environments: Field detection of microplastics using sensors
verified_metadata.abstract: The widespread presence of microplastics in aquatic environments poses a potential threat to ecosystems and human health. Traditional laboratory testing methods suffer from cumbersome procedures, limited temporal and spatial coverage, and high costs. The dynamic changes in microplastic pollution in aquatic environments are challenging to monitor in real time. Therefore, developing efficient on-site detection technologies has become a research priority that urgently needs to be advanced. This paper provides an overview of sensors for the field detection of microplastics in water. First, commonly used microplastic detection methods in experiments were briefly compared. Then, the detection methods are primarily categorized into three types of sensor technologies: optical sensors, electrochemical sensors, and biosensors. The detection principles, technical characteristics, and field application potential of various sensors are systematically outlined. Their advantages and limitations in terms of detection accuracy, anti-interference capability, and other aspects are analyzed in detail. Finally, we further explore how artificial intelligence and microfluidic technology can enhance field testing capabilities. By identifying the current major challenges, this review provides valuable insights into the future development direction of field detection technologies for microplastics in water.

title: Settlements extraction and spatiotemporal analysis with SAM and random forest from high-resolution remote sensing
abstract: The pace of urbanization has accelerated with the implementation of the rural revitalization strategy, thereby intensifying spatial changes in rural settlements. Consequently, accurate and efficient extraction of settlements has become crucial. Current methods often rely on manual calibration, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Remote sensing technology, capable of capturing surface features over a wide range with high accuracy, offers a viable solution. This study utilized high-resolution multisource remote sensing images from the Google Earth Engine (GEE) to extract settlements in Laoling City. A key contribution was the integrated application of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) algorithm and a random forest (RF) classifier for settlement extraction. Finally, the spatiotemporal changes in settlements across 2002, 2012, and 2022 were analyzed. The following results were obtained: (1) July, August, and September were identified as the best classification periods for settlement extraction. (2) Settlement extraction based on the SAM-RF method had the best classification results, with an overall accuracy of 0.98 and a kappa coefficient of 0.97. (3) Most township settlements expanded gradually, with the most remarkable change observed in Shizhong Subdistrict. The remote sensing-based settlement extraction approach in this study is significant for the coordinated development of urban and rural areas. It also provides strong support for the implementation of revitalization, resource management, and environmental protection.

title: Machine learning aided meta-analysis of the impacts of non-biodegradable and biodegradable microplastics on soil microbial communities
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant pollutants in terrestrial ecosystems. However, their impacts on soil microbial communities remain poorly understood. In this study, a comprehensive meta-analysis has been conducted, integrating 1220 paired observations from 64 publications, with a particular focus on comparing the effects of non-biodegradable (Non-bio) and biodegradable (Bio) MPs. Additionally, a machine learning approach has been developed to predict these impacts and identify key contributing factors. Our dual-method approach enables a more precise and comprehensive assessment of MPs’ ecological consequences in soils. The findings revealed that Non-bio MPs reduced microbial diversity by 6.95% but increased microbial biomass and altered community structure by 15.05% and 55.76%, respectively. In contrast, Bio MPs amplified these effects, increasing microbial biomass and community structure by nearly 3.4-fold and 4-fold, respectively. Notably, microbial functions increased by 7.52% under Bio MPs, whereas Non-bio MPs showed no significant impact. Boosted Regression Tree (BRT) analysis identified soil properties (TN, TC, SOC, pH) and MPs characteristics (polymer type, size and concentration) as key drivers of microbial responses. Although Random Forest models achieved reasonable accuracy in predicting the impacts of MPs on microbial diversity and community structure, they performed poorly in predicting microbial functions due to complex and varying enzyme responses. This study highlights the importance of MP biodegradability and underscores the need for longer-term research and comprehensive risk assessments. Future work should prioritize expanded datasets and advanced modeling techniques to unravel the intricate interactions between MPs and soil microbial communities, ultimately supporting more sustainable environment management strategies.

title: Carbon deficit of a megaregion: Spatiotemporal dynamics and interpretable drivers of carbon loss in China's Greater Bay Area
abstract: Rapidly urbanizing megaregions are pivotal for achieving land-based climate-mitigation targets, yet the mechanisms governing their ecosystem carbon dynamics remain poorly understood. In this study, we quantify the spatiotemporal evolution of carbon storage in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), a globally recognized example of rapid coastal urbanization, and diagnose the drivers behind an emerging regional “carbon deficit”. We couple a patch-generating land-use simulation (PLUS) model, a process-based carbon accounting model (InVEST-C), and interpretable machine learning (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to (i) reconstruct land-use and carbon changes from 2000 to 2020 and (ii) project carbon trajectories under three contrasting development pathways to 2030. Total ecosystem carbon storage decreased from 5.45×10 8 Mg in 2000 to 5.11×10 8 Mg in 2020, with the loss rate during 2010–2020 being 18 times higher than during 2000–2010, coinciding with the phase of megaregional integration. Scenario analysis shows that a business-as-usual “natural development” pathway, which extends 2010–2020 land-use trends without additional policy constraints, would lead to a further loss of 2.79×10 7 Mg by 2030. In contrast, a policy-driven sustainable development pathway, which constrains construction-land expansion through urban growth boundaries and ecological conservation redlines and actively promotes ecological restoration, could avoid more than 83% of this potential decline. SHAP-based interpretation reveals that topography provides the essential natural capital for carbon storage, whereas population pressure is the decisive driver of loss. We further identify a strong non-linear interaction in which the ecological cost of urban expansion is greatly amplified on steep, ecologically fragile slopes. Our findings provide a transferable framework for diagnosing carbon deficits in rapidly urbanizing megaregions and deliver spatially explicit evidence to support strict ecological conservation redlines (ECRs) and urban growth boundaries (UGBs) that reconcile urban development with climate and ecological resilience.

title: An integrative framework for avian eggshell coloration: From molecular regulation to phenotypic evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Avian eggshell coloration provides a useful model for connecting evolutionary ecology with poultry genetics, but studies have yet to integrate molecular regulation and phenotypic evolution into a unified framework. This review identifies the conserved heme pathway involving 5’-Aminolevulinate Synthase 1, Ferrochelatase, and Heme Oxygenase 1 as the metabolic basis for protoporphyrin IX and biliverdin deposition and the resulting continuum of shell colors. Eggshell coloration is therefore treated as a multilevel trait governed by genomic architecture, the shell-gland microenvironment, epigenetic regulation, nutrition, and physiological stress. Blue-green coloration is largely stabilized by major-effect genes, whereas brown and speckled phenotypes show stronger polygenic control and genotype-by-environment interactions. These regulatory differences may explain why blue shells are more evolutionarily conserved while brown phenotypes remain more responsive to environmental conditions, with each mode carrying distinct constraints and physiological costs. Key research priorities include single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, interactions between epigenetic regulation and the microbiota, comparative genomics of convergent phenotypes, and the use of artificial intelligence in multi-omics breeding.

title: LLM-assisted multichannel similarity fusion versus supervised deep learning for Raman-based early detection of citrus huanglongbing with metabolomic validation
abstract: ABSTRACT Timely detection of citrus Huanglongbing (HLB) during its prolonged asymptomatic phase remains critical for epidemic management, yet current molecular diagnostics require destructive sampling and extended turnaround. This study presents a non-destructive diagnostic framework integrating handheld Raman spectroscopy, targeted metabolomics, and a large language model-assisted multichannel spectral similarity fusion (LAMSSF) framework benchmarked against supervised deep learning for few-shot early diagnosis. Raman spectra from 1030 Thai pomelo and 480 Wogan mandarin leaves reveal consistent spectral patterns across healthy, early HLB, symptomatic HLB, and nutrient deficiency groups. High-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry validation identifies progressive accumulation of p-coumaric acid, glucose, and L-glutamate as the biochemical basis for these signatures, reflecting phenylpropanoid defense activation, phloem transport impairment, and nitrogen metabolic reprogramming, respectively. While a convolutional neural network (CNN)-Transformer achieves the highest accuracy of 94.8% via cross-cultivar fine-tuning, it requires extensive quantitative PCR-annotated data. In contrast, the proposed LAMSSF framework attains comparable accuracy of 92.2% at equivalent data scales while generating transparent diagnostic reports. Critically, LAMSSF maintains above 90% accuracy with only 24 Thai pomelo and 12 Wogan samples as the training data, a data regime where the CNN-Transformer requires 8.3-fold and 10.0-fold more annotations to match performance. This study demonstrates that while deep learning yields marginal accuracy gains given abundant data, the proposed LAMSSF framework enables scalable, few-shot early HLB diagnosis with minimal annotation requirements and significantly greater field deployment potential.

verified_metadata.title: LLM-assisted multichannel similarity fusion versus supervised deep learning for Raman-based early detection of citrus huanglongbing with metabolomic validation
verified_metadata.abstract: Timely detection of citrus Huanglongbing (HLB) during its prolonged asymptomatic phase remains critical for epidemic management, yet current molecular diagnostics require destructive sampling and extended turnaround. This study presents a non-destructive diagnostic framework integrating handheld Raman spectroscopy, targeted metabolomics, and a large language model-assisted multichannel spectral similarity fusion (LAMSSF) framework benchmarked against supervised deep learning for few-shot early diagnosis. Raman spectra from 1030 Thai pomelo and 480 Wogan mandarin leaves reveal consistent spectral patterns across healthy, early HLB, symptomatic HLB, and nutrient deficiency groups. High-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry validation identifies progressive accumulation of p-coumaric acid, glucose, and L-glutamate as the biochemical basis for these signatures, reflecting phenylpropanoid defense activation, phloem transport impairment, and nitrogen metabolic reprogramming, respectively. While a convolutional neural network (CNN)-Transformer achieves the highest accuracy of 94.8% via cross-cultivar fine-tuning, it requires extensive quantitative PCR-annotated data. In contrast, the proposed LAMSSF framework attains comparable accuracy of 92.2% at equivalent data scales while generating transparent diagnostic reports. Critically, LAMSSF maintains above 90% accuracy with only 24 Thai pomelo and 12 Wogan samples as the training data, a data regime where the CNN-Transformer requires 8.3-fold and 10.0-fold more annotations to match performance. This study demonstrates that while deep learning yields marginal accuracy gains given abundant data, the proposed LAMSSF framework enables scalable, few-shot early HLB diagnosis with minimal annotation requirements and significantly greater field deployment potential.

title: CropRowSeg: A lightweight model for seedling crop row image segmentation combining multi-scale CNN and transformer
abstract: Crop row visual perception can provide navigation information for autonomous row-following equipment and its bottleneck is how to segment target crop rows from complex field images. Existing methods are often designed for specific scenarios or crops, suffering from complex hyperparameter tuning, large parameter sizes, high computational costs, poor convergence, and weak generalization. Departing from traditional row-by-row segmentation, we treat target crop rows aligned with the navigation path as foreground, while categorizing weeds, soil, and other rows as background, establishing an efficient annotation method. We propose CropRowSeg, a semantic segmentation model based on an encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder integrates parallel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) branches with hierarchical feature fusion, enabling local detail perception and global context modeling to address long-range dependencies. In the ViT branch, computational redundancy is reduced via feature dimensionality reduction and spatial-channel decoupled convolution, along with local feature enhancement. A hybrid attention adaptively calibrates feature importance across spatial and channel dimensions. The decoder employs a progressive architecture combining residual connections and coordinate attention to reconstruct details and mitigate information loss during upsampling. We introduce a special loss function to address foreground-background imbalance and spatial confusion between symmetrical rows. Experiments on a diverse crop row dataset demonstrate that CropRowSeg achieves accurate segmentation across environments, growth stages, and crop varieties, showing strong generalization. With only 6.91 M parameters and 12.06 Giga Floating-point Operations Per Second (GFLOPs), the model attains an mIoU of 82.55%, a Recall of 92.75%, and an F1-score of 90.26%. The improved model performance will support deployment on edge devices and promote practical applications.

title: β-Mannanases as versatile biocatalysts: Expression, properties, engineering, and applications in mannose-based prebiotic production
abstract: β-Mannanases are pivotal biocatalysts that hydrolyze mannans into mannose-based prebiotics, including manno-oligosaccharides and partially hydrolyzed mannans, which serve as emerging prebiotics with significant health benefits. This review provides a comprehensive overview of β-mannanases, covering their diverse sources, structural characteristics, heterologous expression systems, and biochemical properties. Recent advances in β-mannanase engineering strategies, including rational design and directed evolution, are highlighted to demonstrate enhanced catalytic efficiency, thermostability, pH adaptability, and hydrolysis properties for industrial applications. Special emphasis is placed on the enzymatic production of mannose-based prebiotics, focusing on substrate selection, specific β-mannanases, and production approaches. The synthesis of these advances bridges fundamental enzymology with industrial practice, providing a comprehensive framework for β-mannanase selection and engineering while outlining strategic pathways for the efficient bioproduction of prebiotics from both conventional and sustainable feedstocks. Furthermore, it outlines emerging trends, such as AI-assisted enzyme design and the utilization of mannan-rich waste streams, providing a roadmap for future research and commercialization in this rapidly advancing field.

title: Advancements in leaf-scale radiative transfer modeling: A review with focus on the PROSPECT model
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf biochemical parameters is fundamental to understanding the physiological status of terrestrial vegetation at the leaf level. Leaf radiative transfer models (RTMs) provide an important theoretical basis for establishing the relationship between leaf spectral information and biochemical information, which simulates the radiative transfer processes and light interaction mechanisms within vegetation. As the most widely used leaf-scale RTM, the PROSPECT model can accurately simulate leaf spectral reflectance and transmittance by inputting leaf structural parameters and physical and chemical parameters. When combined with inversion technologies, RTMs can retrieve the biochemical parameters and leaf structure information of vegetation. It is of great significance to comprehensively review the application of RTMs in leaf spectral simulation and biochemical parameter inversion. The purpose of this paper is to review the development and applications of existing RTMs, focusing on the evolution of the PROSPECT model. The results show that the assumption of a uniform distribution inside the leaf is not completely realistic. Current understanding of leaf internal anatomy remains inadequate. In terms of inversion, physics-based RTMs are still underexplored. Furthermore, RTM inversion studies focused on dominant pigments such as chlorophyll, while carotenoids and anthocyanins received little attention due to their relatively low content.

title: Comprehensive performance evaluation of YOLOv12, YOLO11, YOLOv10, YOLOv9 and YOLOv8 on detecting and counting fruitlet in complex orchard environments
abstract: Object detection, specifically fruitlet detection, is a crucial image processing technique in agricultural automation, enabling the accurate identification of fruitlets on orchard trees within images. It is vital for early fruit load management and overall crop management, facilitating the effective deployment of automation and robotics to optimize orchard productivity and resource use. This study systematically performed an extensive evaluation of the performances of all configurations of YOLOv8, YOLOv9, YOLOv10, and YOLO11 object detection algorithms in terms of precision, recall, mean Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (mAP@50), and computational speeds including pre-processing, inference, and post-processing times immature green apple (or fruitlet) detection in commercial orchards. Additionally, this research performed and validated in-field counting of fruitlets using an iPhone and machine vision sensors in 4 different apple varieties (Scifresh, Scilate, Honeycrisp & Cosmic crisp). This investigation of total 22 different configurations of YOLOv8, YOLOv9, YOLOv10 and YOLO11 (5 for YOLOv8, 6 for YOLOv9, 6 for YOLOv10, and 5 for YOLO11) revealed that YOLOv9 gelan-base and YOLO11s outperforms all other configurations of YOLOv10 , YOLOv9 and YOLOv8 in terms of mAP@50 with a score of 0.935 and 0.933 respectively. In terms of precision, specifically, YOLOv9 Gelan-e achieved the highest mAP@50 of 0.935, outperforming YOLOv11s's 0.0.933, YOLOv10s's 0.924, and YOLOv8s's 0.924. In terms of recall, YOLOv9 gelan-base achieved highest value among YOLOv9 configurations (0.899), and YOLO11m performed the best among the YOLO11 configurations (0.897). In comparison for inference speeds, YOLO11n demonstrated fastest inference speeds of only 2.4 ms, while the fastest inference speed across YOLOv10, YOLOv9 and YOLOv8 were 5.5, 11.5 and 4.1 ms for YOLOv10n, YOLOv9 gelan-s and YOLOv8n respectively.

verified_metadata.abstract:
Abstract

This study systematically conducted an extensive real-world evaluation of all configurations of You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based object detection algorithms, including YOLOv8, YOLOv9, YOLOv10, YOLO11, and YOLOv12. Models were assessed using precision, recall, mean Average Precision at 50 % Intersection over Union (mAP@50), and computational efficiency across pre-processing, inference, and post-processing stages for detecting immature green fruitlets in commercial orchards. Field-level fruitlet counting was also validated using images captured with both Intel RealSense and iPhone 14 Pro Max sensors. YOLOv12l achieved the highest recall (0.900), while YOLOv10x and YOLOv9 GELAN-c reported the top precision scores of 0.908 and 0.903, respectively. YOLOv9 GELAN-base and GELAN-e achieved the highest mAP@50 (0.935), followed by YOLO11s (0.933) and YOLOv12l (0.931). In counting validation, YOLO11n demonstrated superior accuracy, with RMSE values of 4.51–4.96 and MAE values of 3.85–7.73 across four apple varieties. Sensor-specific training on Intel RealSense further improved detection performance. YOLO11n also recorded the fastest inference speed (2.4 ms), outperforming YOLOv8n, YOLOv9 GELAN-s, YOLOv10n, and YOLOv12n, affirming its suitability for real-time orchard applications.

title: Advances in computer vision-based detection and management of greenhouse pests and diseases: A review
abstract: As pressure on global food security mounts, controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) demands innovations in monitoring and control. This review surveys computer-vision methods for greenhouse pests and diseases, covering foundations, core techniques, and applications, highlighting early detection, multimodal fusion, and decision support. We trace the evolution from traditional machine vision to AI-driven methods, spanning image acquisition and preprocessing, feature extraction, and semantic understanding. Deep-learning-based pest and disease recognition improves accuracy under controlled conditions, and enables earlier detection of small-target pests and incipient diseases. Multimodal fusion and transfer learning further improve model generalization in complex greenhouse scenes. We also explore computer vision-driven intelligent decision-making systems, including disease and pest assessment, precision intervention, and optimization of integrated prevention and control strategies. Case studies indicate that AI-based vision systems can provide pest and disease warnings several days in advance, which reduces pesticide use and improves production efficiency. However, bottlenecks such as insufficient environmental adaptability, difficulties in learning from small samples, and limited computational resources still hinder broader implementation. Future research should prioritize multisource heterogeneous data fusion, lightweight model design, and the integration of agronomic knowledge. Together, these directions can support monitoring from phenotypes to mechanisms and from individual plants to populations.

title: A PSO-CatBoost algorithm based on soil sensor data: A novel in-situ intelligent method for estimating field capacity
abstract: ABSTRACT Field capacity (FC) is a key parameter for smart irrigation, but it still requires manual measurement, which limits technological progress. Enhancing the in-situ intelligent analysis capability of soil moisture sensors is crucial for advancing this field. Among 11 common tree-based models, Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) achieved the best performance in FC simulation. Therefore, CatBoost combined with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was employed for parameter optimization, resulting in a data-driven intelligent online FC measurement method. This approach dynamically characterizes soil moisture recession curves at various depths using sensor data, while improving temporal resolution and reducing the complexity of FC estimation. Using a dataset comprising 118 farmland soil moisture monitoring points from major grain-producing regions in China, the proposed method was validated through simulation. The simulation errors were compared with those from other emerging integrated algorithm models, and the results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved superior performance. When applied to FC simulation, the model achieves a remarkably high coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.99, with mean absolute error (MAE) ranging from 0.41% to 1.35%, mean squared error (MSE) from 0.63% to 7.27%, and root mean squared error (RMSE) from 0.80% to 2.64%, respectively. These results confirm that integrating AI with soil sensors enables accurate, in-situ FC estimation. In practice, this method enables dynamic adjustment of irrigation thresholds, supporting automated decision-making and precision water management in modern agriculture.

title: Dynamic analysis of canopy coverage traits and their genetic basis in wheat under multiple environments
abstract: The extent of canopy coverage (CC) prior to the booting stage is a useful indicator of environmental adaptation and may help anticipate key developmental events such as heading and flowering. We used UAV-based high-throughput phenotyping to monitor CC in a 262-line F 8 recombinant inbred line population grown under four irrigation-year environments across two seasons. To quantify CC dynamics, we fitted regression models using either days after sowing (DAS) or accumulated active temperature (AT). These models showed a high goodness-of-fit (overall coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) > 0.90 across environments; per-timepoint prediction R 2 = 0.60‒0.99 with root mean squared error (RMSE) = 0.00‒0.02) and were used to derive 31 CC-related traits. Principal component analysis (PCA) showed that the first two components explained 80.00% of total variance in CC traits, with PCA1 accounting for 48.88%‒62.51% of the variance for DAS-based traits and 50.26%‒54.93% for AT-based traits. PCA1 reflected early canopy vigor and rapid coverage increase, while PCA2 reflected canopy maintenance after jointing. Genotypes in the top 15% for PCA1 differed significantly in flowering time, heading time, and plant height from those in the bottom 15%. Cross-environment comparisons showed moderate to high consistency of CC traits (average correlation ( r ) = 0.41‒0.65 for DAS-standardized CC of 20‒160 DAS and 0.48‒0.67 for AT-standardized CC of 100‒1000 AT). Using CC features derived from both DAS and AT, we trained a random forest model to predict flowering time, highlighting the contribution of both temporal and thermal information to predictive accuracy. This model achieved an independent test set R 2 of 0.81 with an RMSE of 1.25 days within the current dataset. All 31 CC-derived traits were also used for QTL mapping. Inclusive composite interval mapping identified 156 QTL detection events across 15 chromosomes (0.80%‒27.70% phenotypic variance explained), which were consolidated into 26 QTL regions, including loci such as QCC.caas.7A (671.47‒680.09 Mb on 7A) and QCC.caas.5D2 (426.67‒459.42 Mb on 5D). Several of these regions co-localized with previously reported genes associated with tillering, flowering time, winter hardiness and plant height. These findings indicate that CC, characterized by DAS- and AT-based traits, is genetically tractable and predictive of flowering within the current dataset, supporting its potential as a phenology-related trait for wheat improvement. Further validation across broader environments, years, and genetic backgrounds will be needed before broader application.

title: A state-of-the-art review on carbon-based nanomaterials for engineering applications
abstract: Without a comprehensive examination of the available literature on carbon-based nanomaterials (CBNs) across various engineering contexts and dimensions, the field is left vulnerable to a disproportionate focus on specific application requirements or conditions, curtailing the ability to leverage the multifunctionality and interdisciplinary advantages of CBNs. Carbon-based nanocomposites serve as a pivotal conduit for the extensive utilization of CBNs. Their functional performance is commonly tailored through approaches such as functional modification, doping, interface engineering, and multiscale structural design. A systematic discussion is presented on the current design strategies of nanocomposites incorporating carbon dots (CDs), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and graphene-based nanomaterials (GBNs). Representative cases illustrate their significant engineering application potential in five rapidly evolving and highly active fields: electronic devices, energy storage, civil engineering, water treatment, and biomedical engineering. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in CBNs, emphasizing key applications, ongoing challenges, and emerging research opportunities across diverse domains. Interdisciplinary collaboration is poised to further drive innovation, particularly in areas such as energy storage, structural health monitoring, and biosensing. Future advancements are expected to focus on advanced material design, sustainable and scalable fabrication, intelligent optimization using artificial intelligence, interdisciplinary collaboration, and systematic validation to overcome challenges in synthesis, performance, commercialization, and integration. These insights collectively underscore the pivotal role of CBNs in shaping multifunctional, cross-cutting solutions for next-generation engineering systems.

title: Advancing sustainability: circular economy strategies for fibrous polymer composites
abstract: • Comparative assessment of mechanical, thermal, and chemical recycling reveals clear trade-offs in fiber recovery and energy demand. • Life cycle evaluation shows recycled HDPE, PET, and carbon fibers outperform virgin materials in cost and environmental impact under policy incentives. • Hybrid recycling with process control achieves ∼90% fiber quality retention while reducing overall processing costs. • AI- and IoT-enabled monitoring improves traceability, process efficiency, and circular-economy performance. Fibrous polymer composites are widely used in aerospace, automotive, and renewable energy due to their lightweight and high-strength properties. Traditional linear production and disposal methods, however, cause resource depletion and environmental impacts. This review critically synthesizes circular economy strategies for fibrous polymer composites, integrating material selection, additive manufacturing, and recycling pathways. Mechanical, thermal, and chemical recycling methods are compared in terms of fiber recovery (60–90%), energy consumption (0.5–5.0 MJ/kg), and economic feasibility, highlighting trade-offs between efficiency and scalability. Agro-based and synthetic fibers are evaluated for their performance and sustainability potential. Implementable strategies such as design-for-disassembly, hybrid recycling, AI-driven material traceability, and policy–industry collaboration are discussed to enhance circularity. By providing a systems-level framework linking composite design, end-of-life management, and industrial application, this review identifies critical research gaps, informs sustainable composite development, and offers policy-relevant guidance to promote environmental and economic benefits. By emphasizing recycling, renewable fibers, and resource-efficient design, this study supports the advancement of cleaner, more sustainable composite materials.

title: Optimizing rubberized Concrete: Machine learning insights into effects of particle size on the compressive strength
abstract: End-of-life tires (ELTs) are a persistent solid waste stream worldwide, posing significant challenges to sustainable waste management. Incorporating crumb rubber (CR) derived from ELTs into concrete offers a promising recycling pathway; however, the complex interactions among CR particle size, aggregate replacement ratio, and water-to-cementitious (w/cm) ratio make compressive strength prediction and mix optimization challenging using conventional experimental approaches alone. This study develops a Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) based machine learning (ML) framework trained on a comprehensive dataset of 909 data points compiled from 58 peer-reviewed studies. The CatBoost model achieved the highest predictive accuracy among eight evaluated models, with a test R 2 of 92.2% and RMSE of 4.7 MPa. verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed TVAE and probabilistic learning for uncertainty-aware prediction of tensile strength and moisture susceptibility in sustainable asphalt mixtures
verified_metadata.abstract: Tensile cracking and moisture-induced damage remain persistent challenges in asphalt pavements, particularly when recycled asphalt shingles (RAS) are incorporated to enhance material circularity. These challenges are exacerbated by material heterogeneity and limited experimental datasets, which constrain reliable performance assessment. This study introduces a novel hybrid framework that integrates physics-informed tabular variational autoencoder (PI-TVAE)-generated synthetic data with probabilistic machine learning models to predict indirect tensile strength in dry conditions (ITSD) and tensile strength ratio (TSR), capturing both cracking resistance and moisture susceptibility of RAS-modified asphalt mixtures. Unlike conventional data-driven augmentation methods, PI-TVAE preserves physically meaningful relationships among material variables, enabling statistically consistent and uncertainty-aware predictions. When combined with natural gradient boosting, the proposed framework achieves high predictive accuracy with well-calibrated confidence intervals, outperforming Bayesian neural networks in uncertainty quantification. Explainable AI analysis further identifies aggregate gradation, air voids, volumetric properties, and rejuvenator content as key drivers of tensile performance and moisture resistance. By reducing dependence on extensive laboratory testing while improving predictive reliability, this framework supports data-efficient evaluation and sustainable design of RAS asphalt pavements. The accompanying web-based decision-support tool enables rapid, uncertainty-informed material assessment, advancing cleaner and more resilient pavement engineering.

title: Image-driven feature mining for elastic modulus prediction in asphalt concrete
abstract: Asphalt concrete (AC) is a heterogeneous aggregate–mortar material whose effective mechanical properties are strongly governed by mesostructural geometry and constituent material properties. Establishing quantitative relationships between real mesostructures and the elastic modulus is important for reducing experimental cost and improving material design efficiency. This study proposes an image-driven forward prediction and inverse analysis framework for elastic modulus evaluation of AC based on real mesostructural images. A mesostructural image sample generation algorithm is developed to expand realistic datasets derived from computed tomography (CT) images, and an automated image-based finite element (FE) modeling framework is established to generate elastic modulus labels. By integrating real mesostructural geometry, constituent material properties, and FE analysis, an offline mesostructural image–elastic modulus database is constructed. Based on this database, a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based prediction method is developed to efficiently estimate the elastic modulus of independent AC mesostructures, while a gradient-based inverse analysis method is introduced to identify key mesoscopic geometric contributors. The results show that the proposed framework enables efficient mapping from real mesostructural images to the elastic modulus and provides interpretable information on the effects of global and local mesostructural variations. By reducing reliance on repeated specimen preparation and mechanical testing, the proposed method can decrease material consumption, testing costs, and experimental waste, thereby supporting cleaner and more resource-efficient AC material design.
